version.changelog:
sync: v1.0.3 — 中文名 AI 钥匙；套件二改名生意操盘手

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

llm.summary: This is a disclosed content/business routing skill with some local discovery and memory behavior, but I found no deception, exfiltration, destructive action, or hidden privilege escalation.

dimensions.detail: The helper script reads local skill directories under ~/.claude/skills and ~/.agents/skills and prints installed aikey skill names, descriptions, and real paths; this is purpose-aligned for routing but exposes local installation layout to the agent.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package contains Markdown instructions/references and one simple bash helper; there are no install hooks, remote payload fetches, dependencies, or bundled executable persistence mechanisms.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Some trigger phrases are broad and could invoke the skill for generic video/help requests, but the runtime instructions repeatedly constrain it to routing, prompt generation, onboarding, or post-task navigation rather than executing unrelated work.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Shared family instructions describe reading and writing configured vault memory and output files; this is disclosed and scoped to the content system, but users should understand it may create or update local records when used in a configured vault.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill coherently acts as an AI KEY entry point for routing content and business tasks, onboarding users, and handing off to aikey-* skills; it also references account data, config, and memory as part of that workflow.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install this if you want an aikey-family router that can inspect installed aikey skills and use a configured local content vault. Before using it in a sensitive workspace, confirm you are comfortable with it reading configured content/memory paths and creating or updating local memory/output files as part of the workflow.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: The broad activation phrases are real, but they match the advertised role as a general entry point for users who do not know which content/business skill to use; this is an invocation-quality concern, not evidence of malicious behavior.
[AE1] expected: The referenced-file concern appears to stem from path aliases such as aikey/references/...; the local package includes the corresponding references, and I inspected the available referenced files. I did not find analysis-evasion behavior.
[SDI-2] expected: The skill does instruct the agent to run a local discovery script, but the script is read-only, restricted to aikey-family skill discovery, and directly supports the router purpose.
[SQP-3] expected: The plain-language and citation-style instructions are communication defaults for this Chinese-language skill family, and the main skill explicitly says to reply in the user's language; this does not amount to a hidden hostile output override.
[SDI-4] expected: The onboarding option that continues into Mode A still routes through Mode A steps that end with prompt generation; I found ambiguity worth documenting, but not an unsafe automatic downstream execution path.
[SDI-1] expected: Installed-skill enumeration is broader than a static table, but it is disclosed, read-only, and falls back to static routing if unavailable; users should be aware it reveals local skill paths to the agent.
[SQP-3] expected: The bash helper's messages are Chinese-only, consistent with the surrounding skill package; this is a localization/usability issue rather than a security concern.
